language_routing.hold: Document-like royal notices occur before the language switch; form is not inferred from language alone.
The switch supports dossier and document seams but does not by itself require one chunk or decide chronology.
The Passover closure and Ezra introduction are distinct functional units despite continuous Hebrew.
The royal commission is preserved as a full embedded document.
Language continuity does not erase memoir, prayer, assembly, investigation, and register seams.

translation_and_document_holds: Persian royal names, titles, dates, offices, measures, weights, monetary terms, and Beyond-the-River vocabulary
Aramaic letter superscriptions, salutations, accusations, archive-search formulas, legal prohibitions, and penalty formulas
Hebrew and Aramaic qere/ketiv evidence is witness metadata, not a preferred-reading decision
Nethinim/temple-servant, priestly genealogy, holy-seed, foreign-women, guilt, covenant, oath, and dismissal terminology
First-person and third-person transitions near 7:27 and through chapters 8-10
Cyrus, Ahasuerus, Artaxerxes, and Darius references cannot be arranged into an authorized imperial chronology by chunking

hardest_passages.why: retrospective notices, Hebrew-Aramaic switch, nested letters, archive memorandum, decree, narrative enforcement, and imperial chronology pressure create several defensible macro and document seam systems
genealogy and journey introduction, Hebrew copy formula, Aramaic commission, and Hebrew first-person doxology create language, voice, and document attachment alternatives

report, embodied response, confession, proposal, oath, summons, assembly, investigation, and register may be modeled at several coherent scales while carrying high translation and doctrinal misuse risk
